prospect.name: DJ Hayden
prospect.occupation: Registered Nurse by training, currently in a clinical support rather than bedside role — charting, chart review and project management. Sits for a good majority of the day.
prospect.family_status: Married; his wife does the grocery shopping. Two young sons, one four and a half turning five in November and one just turned one. Keeps chickens in the backyard for eggs.
prospect.training_background: Cross-country and track in high school, weightlifting continued through college, martial arts. Currently trains three to four times a week — Brazilian jiu-jitsu two to three times plus another class once or twice. Describes his weightlifting history as 'pretty traditional'. Has followed Trevor on Instagram for a little over a year and has been trying his kettlebell workouts. Targets about 7,000 steps a day and usually gets close. Has never worked with a coach; has previously bought prepaid workout plans to follow on his own.
prospect.medical: Explicitly denies anything chronic or diagnosed. 'My shoulders aren't great' and a left elbow tweaked one or two weeks earlier doing jiu-jitsu. Frames it as accumulated wear: 'I was an active young kid, and abused my body, and I just kind of deal with the aches and pains of getting older... I don't have, like, a chronic slip disc or anything like that.' Reports finding it hard to get up and moving in the mornings and a slump around lunch. Notably, the presenting complaint is cognitive rather than physical — significant mental fog after intellectually demanding days.

Accepted the good-to-great framing without demur when the rep put it to him
Confidence held down at 0.75 because the recording truncates before price, so the defining test of the archetype — whether price reads as a quality signal or a barrier — is never observable

goals.text: Consolidate conditioning, endurance, strength and mobility into one session instead of a different workout for each
Have energy left for two young sons at the end of the day rather than giving them the leftovers
Improve general fitness to support Brazilian jiu-jitsu
Keep considering himself an athlete, not merely in shape
Learn what to actually do with kettlebells — 'I don't feel like I really know what I would be doing with them to optimize things'
Play the long game and still be doing all of it with his kids years from now

pains.text: Mental fog after intellectually demanding workdays — 'when I get home, there's just a lot of mental fog that I have to try to battle through'
Not enough time to train each quality separately — conditioning, endurance, strength and mobility all compete
Worried his kids get the leftovers of his energy rather than the best of it
No idea how to programme kettlebells despite enjoying them; traditional lifting background only
Sluggish getting going in the mornings and a reliable energy dip around lunch
Shoulders 'aren't great' and a recently tweaked left elbow from jiu-jitsu
Sedentary for the majority of the workday since moving off the bedside

offer.guarantee_mentioned: "there is also a guarantee from Trevor on what he does that in those six months, you will add at least eight kilos, which is around 17 pounds to the baseline weight of the kettlebells, the core kettlebells movements. And that combined with proper nutrition gets you to your goal. It's just pure science behind that."

It never came back. When the rep did later ask the right question — 'do you feel like there's something left on the table right now?' — the prospect gave a genuinely useful answer about mental fog, and that was dropped too.
